newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open slightly higher.

text.p: Singapore shares opened slightly firmer on Thursday in a continued technical correction to earlier big losses and on the back of a record overnight close on Wall Street, dealers said.
"The market is on a technical rebound. I don't see much bargain hunting at the moment," one dealer with a local broking house said.
The Straits Times Industrial Index at 0145 GMT was up 1.5 points to 2,072.76 points.
Dealers said that property counters were leading the market up but trading remained thin.
The new Business Times Singapore Regional Index (SRI) at 0145 GMT was down 5.16 points or 0.52 percent to 978.06 points.
Debut share CM Telecom was among the most actively traded shares with 2.38 million shares traded at 0150 GMT. The counter opened to trade at US$0.37, up from its IPO price of US$0.32.
Overall volume was 22.24 million shares traded with gainers ahead of losers 58 to 20.
